questions.q: From which country did Mauritius gain independence in 1968?
questions.why: It became a republic in 1992.

questions.q: Which three European powers ruled Mauritius?
questions.why: It is named after Maurice of Nassau.

questions.q: Who was the first Prime Minister of Mauritius?
questions.why: He is called the father of the nation.

questions.q: Which island group did Britain separate from Mauritius before independence?
questions.why: The UK agreed in 2025 to hand it over.

questions.q: Which mountain was a refuge for runaway slaves?
questions.why: It is a UNESCO site.

questions.q: Which famous stamps from 1847 are among the rarest in the world?
questions.why: There are only a few left.

questions.q: Which 1810 battle was Napoleon's only naval win on the Arc de Triomphe?
questions.why: Britain took the island months later.

questions.q: What is the capital of Mauritius?
questions.why: It is a busy port.

questions.q: Which ocean is Mauritius in?
questions.why: It lies east of Madagascar.

questions.q: Which immigration depot for indentured workers is a UNESCO site?
questions.why: Indian workers arrived there from 1834.

questions.q: Which island is an autonomous part of Mauritius?
questions.why: It is about 560 km to the east.

questions.q: Which colourful sand dunes are in Chamarel?
questions.why: The colours do not mix.

questions.q: What causes the 'underwater waterfall' illusion off Le Morne?
questions.a: Sand and silt flowing down an underwater slope
questions.why: It is best seen from a seaplane.

questions.q: Which crater lake is sacred to Hindus on Mauritius?
questions.why: Pilgrims walk there for Maha Shivaratri.

questions.q: Which national park protects the island's native forest?
questions.why: It has rare pink pigeons.

questions.q: Which giant tortoises live on Mauritius's reserves today?
questions.why: They replace extinct native kinds.

questions.q: Which island off the east coast is a nature reserve for rare birds?
questions.why: The pink pigeon was saved there.

questions.q: Which mountain shaped like a thumb overlooks Port Louis?
questions.why: Its name means 'the thumb'.

questions.q: Which horse-racing course in Port Louis is one of the oldest?
questions.why: It opened in 1812.

questions.q: Which music and dance tradition came from African slaves?
questions.why: It is on UNESCO's list.

questions.q: Who became Prime Minister of Mauritius again in 2024?
questions.why: His alliance won all 60 mainland seats.

questions.q: Which French governor developed Port Louis in the 1730s?
questions.why: A statue of him stands in the city.

questions.q: Which extinct bird lived only on Mauritius?
questions.why: It died out in the late 1600s.

questions.q: Which bird saved from extinction is called the 'pigeon des mares'?
questions.why: It was down to about 10 birds.

questions.q: Which bird was once the world's rarest falcon?
questions.why: Only four were left in 1974.

questions.q: What is Mauritius's currency?
questions.why: Its code is MUR.

questions.q: Which botanical garden has giant water lilies?
questions.why: It is one of the oldest in the Southern Hemisphere.

questions.q: Which language do most Mauritians speak at home?
questions.why: English is official in parliament.

questions.q: Which crop has long been the main crop of Mauritius?
questions.why: Much land is still under cane.

questions.q: Which flatbread snack filled with split peas is sold on the street?
questions.why: It is a favourite lunch.
